reuse.why: All rule changes go into the existing getScheduledAmount and the approximate tolerance reuses getApproxNumberThreshold from shared/rules; the API field calls the same helper.

duplication.why: No copied amount logic; the only repetition is the positional 'false' inverse argument and the operator threaded by hand at each caller.

placement.why: The expected-amount rule stays in shared/schedules.ts; callers in api-models, forecast, schedule-template, schedules/app and Balance only pass their data.

scope.why: Carries unrelated import reordering in server/schedules/app.ts and four release notes, two of which describe superseded rules (midpoint-to-furthest-from-zero) that contradict the final behaviour.

maintainability.why: The new optional amountOp is passed at some callers but not others (shared/schedules.ts preview, SchedulesTable, MobileSchedulesPage, SchedulesListItem, useScheduleEdit), so approximate amounts are planned differently depending on the screen, and the boolean-then-string positional signature is easy to misuse.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every amount site still goes through getScheduledAmount; none re-implements it.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount: the rangeRounding option was replaced by an optional amountOp parameter with an 'isapprox' branch; several existing callers (shared preview at line ~534, SchedulesTable x2, MobileSchedulesPage, SchedulesListItem, useScheduleEdit x2) were left without the operator, so the helper's behaviour now depends on whether each caller remembered to pass it.
